report:
Reviewed the complete owner_binder claim and all six ordinary implementation entries. Requirements are owner-only creation under one binder, reopening in associated-item/field/body queries, adding only genuinely new item parameters, and preserving both existing GenericParam and owner Self identities. CheckGenerics mints type/lifetime/const handles from the current owner Symbol and index. Struct sig owns that call and Binder construction; fields takes self.sig().iter_symbols() rather than invoking CheckGenerics again. Trait sig creates explicit parameters and the sole Self handle (owner parent, reserved index), combines them under one binder, and items reuses its iter_symbols. Impl sig owns header generics and self type; items passes those same symbols into lower_items. Associated lower_items stores the supplied owner handles directly, without minting parameters. Function open_owner copies the owner signature and preserves its GenericParam handles and Self type. Fn sig mints only the function CST generics with the function as parent and appends them after the owner prefix. Fn body reopens its own signature symbols and imports signature types, including owner Self; it does not call CheckGenerics. BinderExt copies handles from the binder slice; Ribs stores those handles unchanged; GenericParam is StashDirect. These paths also handle an empty owner parameter list and free functions without inventing owner identities. The supported non-GAT impl associated-type value path likewise takes impl signature symbols. Broader unsupported associated-type semantics are not claimed as new functionality here.

The ordinary trait_and_impl_signatures_share_complete_generic_binders test visibly checks the trait binder contains Self and T, its one bound is retained and eligible, and the impl binder contains one parameter with equal semantic types for both T occurrences in the tuple self type. Its setup helper constructs a real source-backed local crate. This is meaningful but partial evidence: it would catch binder arity mistakes and unequal tuple parameter references, not independent reconstruction in a field or body query. The explicit checking_signature_owner_binder TODO records exactly the missing trait/impl/associated-function/field/body semantic identity matrix, across queries and revisions with owner/method scopes separated. Accepted as a visible test deferral, not a passing verification: completion requires those fixtures and direct identity comparisons, including owner Self and new method identities. No N/A entries exist. No behavior violation was identified in the inspected paths.

Added the essential owner_binder associations in generics, associated, fns, impls, and traits with coordinator authorization, then restarted and reviewed current inputs after concurrent storage comments settled. Captured generic representation, binder iteration/copy, ribs, signature import, and test setup dependencies using review read. Ran cargo fmt. Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib trait_and_impl_signatures_share_complete_generic_binders: one test passed. An earlier --exact invocation with an unqualified name selected zero tests and is not counted as behavioral validation. Workspace build and delegated post-codegen/sanity reviews remain coordinator checks; this report is a source assessment with the focused execution evidence above.
